dipolar modulation in right ascension at energies above 8 EeV, as previously

(OOK) system over 18.8km dispersion-uncompensated submarine optical cable in
the South China Sea. Chromatic dispersion (CD) of 18.8km submarine optical
cable causes four spectral nulls on the 36GHz bandwidth of 72Gbit/s OOK signal,
which is the main obstacle for achieving an acceptable bit-error-rate (BER)
performance. Decision feedback equalizer (DFE) is effective to compensate for
the spectral nulls. However, DFE has a serious defect of burst-error
propagation when the burst errors emerge due to the unstable submarine
environment. Weighted DFE (WDFE) can be used to mitigate the burst-error
propagation, but it cannot fully compensate for the spectral nulls because only
a part of feedback symbols is directly decided. Fortunately, maximum likelihood
sequence estimation (MLSE) can be added after the WDFE to simultaneously
eliminate the resisting spectral distortions and implement optimal detection.
Compared to the joint DFE and MLSE algorithm, the joint WDFE and MLSE algorithm
can effectively suppress the burst-error propagation to obtain a maximum 2.9dB
improvement of $\boldsymbol{Q}$ factor and eliminate the phenomenon of BER
floor. In conclusion, the joint WDFE and MLSE algorithm can effectively
compensate for the spectral nulls to obtain a maximum 72Gbit/s BER$\leq$1$\times$
10$^{-3}$. Therefore, a maximum data rate of 70.5Gbit/s can be achieved over
18.8km submarine optical cable.

variant of eigenvector centrality
for multilayer networks with inter-layer constraints on node importance.
Specifically, we consider a multilayer network defined by multiple
edge-weighted, potentially directed, graphs over the same set of nodes with
each graph representing one layer of the network and no inter-layer edges. As
in the standard eigenvector centrality construction, the importance of each
node in a given layer is based on the weighted sum of the importance of
adjacent nodes in that same layer. Unlike standard eigenvector centrality, we
assume that the adjacency relationship and the importance of adjacent nodes may
be based on distinct layers. Importantly, this type of centrality constraint is
only partially supported by existing frameworks for multilayer eigenvector
centrality that we are aware of. Our approach relies on a new formulation of a
monotone variant of the nodal constraint eigenvector centrality measure that
we recently introduced, which allows us to capture the type of complex
inter-layer dependencies considered in a study from sociology. Using a novel
relaxed optimization approach, our method can handle directed, anisotropic,
and heterogeneous interactions across the layers as well as unsigned and
signed interactions within each layer. Furthermore, our approach can handle the
general case of different inverse constraints on the importance of the
adjacent nodes in each layer as well as equal constraints, which is not
possible with existing methods. Finally, we show through extensive experiments
on several real datasets that our approach is efficient as it does not require
iterative methods and provides better nodal ranking than other methods,
including those allowed by existing frameworks.
  In conclusion, we introduce a new mathematical formulation of nodal
constraint eigenvector centrality for multilayer networks with complex
inter-layer dependencies that can handle directed, anisotropic, and heterogeneous
interactions. A novel relaxed optimization approach allows us to efficiently
compute the centrality measures for several real datasets, producing better
ranking than other methods.

  Our goal is to minimize the use of trusted components while sandboxing
malicious programs. We present VISA, a hypervisor that allows untrusted
applications to run security-critical programs. VISA uses Hardware Isolated
Execution (HIE) regions to create isolated environments for applications.
Security-critical programs are compiled into HIE regions and executed in
enclaves, which provide strong hardware isolation guarantees similar to that of
Intel SGX enclaves, but with much lower performance overhead.
  We show that most common security programs, including several antivirus
software and malware analysis tools, work correctly in enclaves. We also
demonstrate how an malicious program that breaks out of an enclave attempts to
crash the host computer, and how VISA contains the damage.
  To improve the usability and performance of security programs running in
enclaves, we introduce optimizations that reduce the size of programs while
maintaining their security functionality. For example, our hash verification
security program (which verifies that a file or block of data maps to a
correct hash value) took 1.5x to 3x less space than its reference counterpart.
We also show that our integration of ClamAV antivirus software with a malware
reversing program reduced size by about 30%.
  Our results demonstrate that VISA allows security programs to run safely and
trustlessly on the same machine as malicious programs.

fundamental quantum physics and several applications in metrology, on-chip

generate multi-phonon states through the interaction with an electronic
resonator. In this work, we propose a protocol to quantify the negativity of
the acoustic covariance matrix of a two-mode acoustic cavity. We do so by
sending a spin-triplet of photons with an entangled spin state through a
quantum acoustic cavity and then analyzing the acoustic output. Our approach
can determine the full acoustic covariance matrix and therefore can be used
to quantify any feature of the acoustic two-mode state, including negativity
of the local phonon number variance, two-photon correlation functions and
acoustic entanglement. Our protocol requires absolutely no information about
the parameters of the acoustic cavity, therefore making it semi-universal.
Being exotic and potentially more resilient to decoherence, our protocol could
play a fundamental role in the hybrid path towards multi-phonon entanglement.
Moreover, it can be used in the context of quantum acoustic cavities design and
optimization, therefore making it pratically important.
  We also propose an alternative protocol, which can determine whether the
acoustic cavity is in an entangled state or not, by using two photons with an
unpolarized entangled spin state. This protocol can indicate the presence of
entanglement with only one set of phonon variances, making it more
convenient than the previous one. Both protocols can be relevant for the
development and implementation of hybrid schemes towards multi-phonon physics.
They can also be used in inhomogeneous acoustic environments, therefore making
them useful for the future applications.
  Finally, we show that both protocols can be realized with classical light.
Therefore, they offer an interesting feature that can be of great interest for
the future applications, where only the information contained in the light
structure is what matters.
  All the proposals presented here can be applied to any two-mode acoustic
cavity, therefore making them semi-universal.
  We believe that our works can be fundamental for the development and
implementation of hybrid schemes towards multi-phonon entanglement and quantum
acoustic cavities design and optimization.
  In the latter, the fact that our protocols are semi-universal can be of
great importance, therefore making us to conclude that our proposals are
practically important as well.

problems can be formulated as functional optimization problems with
differential equality and inequality constraints. Since these problems are
infinite-dimensional and often do not have a known analytical solution, one has
to resort to numerical methods to compute an approximate solution. This paper
uses a unifying notation to outline some of the techniques used in the
transcription step of simultaneous direct methods (which
discretize-then-optimize) for solving continuous-time dynamic optimization
problems. We focus on collocation, integrated residual and Runge-Kutta schemes.
These transcription methods are then applied to a simulation case study to
answer a question that arose during the COVID-19 pandemic, namely: If there are
not enough ventilators, is it possible to ventilate more than one patient on a
single ventilator? The results suggest that it is possible, in principle, to
estimate individual patient parameters sufficiently accurately, using a
relatively small number of flow rate measurements, without needing to
disconnect a patient from the system or needing more than one flow rate sensor.
We also show that it is possible to ensure that two different patients can
indeed receive their desired tidal volume, by modifying the resistance
experienced by the air flow to each patient and controlling the ventilator
pressure.
  A supplemental MATLAB code is available that implements the transcription

aforementioned clinical question. It does not contain any novel numerical
algorithms. The code also contains examples of the deep learning approaches
discussed in the recent survey paper [1] for solving the resulting nonlinear
optimization problems that result from collocation. While those methods are
very efficient, they require large datasets of optimal solutions which can be
difficult to compute, especially when the cost function has a large number of
local minima.

ophageal tumor in CT images is known
to be very challenging. This is due to the low contrast between the tumor and
adjacent tissues, the anatomical variation of the esophagus, as well as the
occasional presence of foreign bodies (e.g. feeding tubes). Physicians
therefore usually exploit additional information such as endoscopic images,
barium swallow, and esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) reports. The latter are
ordinarily available only after the primary imaging analysis, which postpones
the delineation task or requires the radiologists to review the images multiple
times. Our aim is to facilitate the daily clinical practice of radiologists
by providing an automatic tumor delineation method on CT images that is
comparable to manual delineations by experts. To achieve this, we introduce a
novel multi-task convolutional neural network (MT-CNN) that simultaneously
solves two tasks: (a) esophagus segmentation and (b) tumor classification.
Thereafter, we use the output of the first task to get the esophageal mask,
and finally apply an instance-segmentation-like approach to obtain the tumor
boundary. We validate our approach on a publicly available CT dataset for
esophageal cancer, which includes both pre-treatment and post-treatment scans.
We show that our approach provides better results compared to previously
published methods, both quantitatively and when validated by expert radiologists
and clinicians.

available CT dataset for esophageal cancer yields both quantitative and
clinical validation improvements over previously published methods.

which the named entities (NEs) are nested with each other. However, most of the
previous studies on nested NER usually apply linear structure to model the
nested NEs which are actually presented in a hierarchical structure. Besides,
most of existing studies usually focus on the English language and do not
consider the characteristics of agglutinative languages like Korean. In order
to fully understand the correct relation modeling in nested NEs and carry out
relatively complete NER research which considers major languages (e.g. English
and Korean), we first and foremost conduct detailed analyses on the NEs in
English and Korean. During the analysis, several incorrect assumptions in
previous studies are discovered according to analysis on corpora and theories
in linguistics. We then propose two methods to model the proper NEs with
reasonable assumptions in a hierarchical structure. Experiments are conducted
on publicly available Korean datasets with comparison to baselines. The
results of our study demonstrate the correctness of analysis on NEs and
effectiveness of proposed methods in Korean NER.

alternatives to reference-based evaluation, namely generation of diverse
description variants, crowdsourced rating of description quality and rating

of image description generation and evaluation. I present the DesignRank
algorithm, a method for evaluating systems based on a semantic alignment
between system and reference descriptions. DesignRank avoids the problems of

image description systems. Thus, I argue that the image description research
community as a whole benefits from careful design of evaluation data and

from which users originated.

explained by the offline media consumption patterns of the areas from which the
users originated, and propose that news -- whether misinformation or not --

an overview of pathwise methods and open questions in the pathwise setting.

which is not available in the literature. They end with a discussion of the
connection to the pathswise approach and the open problems in this direction.

SPDE. Chapter 6 provides an overview of the pathwise approach (with a brief
discussion of the connections to the deterministic flow map) and concludes with

the application of operator theoretic methods to SPDE. Many authors use

creation and control
of high-performance solid-state telecom photon-spin interfaces. Tungsten
monoxide is a semiconductor with promising properties, including a
spectroscopically convenient doped-bandspin valve structure and a
lattice-match to silicon, but as yet there is no established method for
injecting excitons into its bulk material. Here we show that
\textit{inverse} opal tungsten oxide provides both a very high (up to
0.064%) spin-triplet to spin-singlet exciton to photon absorption anisotropy
and room temperature photoluminescence quantum efficiencies of ~1%. Using a
novel combination of X-ray and E-beam lithography, we fabricate the first
vertical $Ci$-shaped Schottky diodes to electrical pump the excitons in the
inverse opal towards 1.5 eV. At 300 K, these devices show a remarkable
\textit{net} 0.8 W/m$^2$ exciton-photon coupling power ($\chi$) and a
\textit{total} coupling power of 1.2 W/m$^2$, giving an exciton-to-photon
trapping efficiency of 71$\%$. Our results make inverse opal tungsten oxide a
viable candidate for the telecom photon-spin interfaces that are required for
global quantum networks.
  We express the anisotropy of exciton absorption in inverse opal semiconductors
in terms of an effective dipole moment per exciton that is coupled to the
photonic stop-band anomaly. We show that this approach may be used to predict
the anisotropy in a wide range of materials, including those that are currently
unstudied because of the experimental challenges of their characterisation.
Moreover, the technique is extended to account for the effects of both
Purcell enhancement and anti-resonant behaviour of the exciton absorption.
Moreover, we find that the exciton anisotropies in many materials could be
economically scaled to at least 0.1% making them suitable for the reliable
creation of high-performance solid-state telecom photon-spin interfaces.
Tungsten oxide has an excess of 2\% of the theoretical limit and materials
such as gallium phosphate and silver halides are a factor of 5 better than what
is currently required.

degenerate Bernoulli polynomial $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ and study the
corresponding degenerate Bernoulli number
$\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,1)=m^{k}\beta_{k}(1/m)$, where $\beta_{k}(\lambda),
\lambda\neq 0$ is the standard degenerate Bernoulli number. Our approach relies
on a new algebraic framework for generating functions and the action of a
symbolic evaluation function on powers of polynomials. We show that
$\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ displays surprising links with other mathematical
objects (such as Circulant matrices and Galois fields) and enjoys many
interesting algebraic, symmetric and dynamical properties that could be
deployed to perform efficient computations.
  In particular, we obtain explicit formulas for the first 16 values of
$\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ as a function of $m$ and $x$, as well as recursive
formulas that are independent of $m$ and $x$, respectively. We also prove that
$\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ enjoys a remarkable determinant formula which is a
manifestation of the remarkable properties of the matrix
$A=diag(I_{m},xI_{m}+A_{0})$. Many additional results are established in the
companion paper \cite{GP20b}.

for {\sc De}generate {\sc B}ernoulli -- for computing
$\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,1)=m^{k}\beta_{k}(1/m)$ in a fast and efficient manner,
even when $m$ is a large integer. This algorithm greatly benefits from the many
algebraic and dynamical properties of $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ that we
established above. As a by-product, it allows us to compute the first 10000
values of $\beta_{k}(1/m)$ for $m\in \{1, 2, \ldots, 10001\}$, as well as the
first 10000 first values of the classical Bernoulli numbers $\beta_{k}(1)$ for
which we can compute exact expressions.

exoplanets, as it introduces spurious jitter in the data sets and prevents the
correct retrieval of a planetary signal. This is key for M dwarfs, considering
that they manifest high levels of activity and are primary targets for present
and future searches of habitable Earth-like planets. Effective filtering of
activity is crucial to achieve the sensitivity required for the detection of
much weaker planetary signals. In this work we compare the performance of four
different indices in selecting active days and plans to assess their
consistency with an independent measure of activity. We apply the indices to
more than 5000 light measurements of the active M dwarf EV Lac obtained with
VPHAS+ in the visible and with the TESS satellite in the near ultraviolet during
a 200-day observing run. We evaluate the effectiveness of each selected frame
in the visible to be active according to the $\hbox{EW}_2$ index, which
retains $\geq 70\%$ of the expected variability for an $\hbox{EW}_2$ threshold
of $-6.0$ \AA. We also find that $\geq 80\%$ of the selected frames with
$\hbox{EW}_2> -5.0$ \AA\ present activity levels above the median $\hbox{MW}
\geq 0.5$. Conversely, a Doppler Activity Index (DAI) threshold of 2.0 does not
exclude activity in 30% of the cases and selects active episodes 5 months
before they are clearly visible in the $\hbox{EW}_2$ light curve. The
Stellar Activity Index (SAI) of TESS frames in the near UV is a function of the
visible activity in the preceding days, providing a long activity persistence
of active episodes for $\geq 40$ days and a correlation between the visible and
near UV activity with a slope of $1.3$. Finally, we find that a correlation
between the activity and the rotational period, as previously reported for some
other stars, is not present in the data.
  Based on the results, we conclude that $\hbox{EW}_2$ is the best activity
indicator for the VPHAS+ visible bands, while the DAI is the best in the near
UV. Although the SAI does not provide information on the activity levels, the
data show that it is a robust indicator of activity

been implemented in TinyOS 2.1, and evaluated in a testbed using TelosB motes.

object detectors exploit scene context for recognition differently. In this
paper, we group object detectors into 3 categories in terms of context use: no
context by cropping the input (RCNN), partial context by cropping the
featuremap (two-stage methods) and full context without any cropping
(single-stage methods). We systematically evaluate the effect of context for
each deep detector category. We create a fully controlled dataset for varying
context and investigate the context for deep detectors. We also evaluate
gradually removing the background context and the foreground object on MS COCO.
We demonstrate that single-stage and two-stage object detectors can and will
use the context by virtue of their large receptive field. Thus, choosing the
best object detector may depend on the application context.
  We provide a new perspective on object detector comparison based on the
exploited context and propose a new metric, context sensitivity metric
(CSM). CSM is a robust evaluation metric for object detectors on varying
context. We provide a new benchmark, CCME (context sensitivity benchmark for
object detectors), with 5 different contexts on MS COCO. Following the
benchmark, we present a comprehensive study on how different object detectors
perform on contexts. Among all studies, RCNN and FAN do not work as others on
contexts. FAN gets the highest score on low context and RCNN gets the highest
score on high context from CSM. FAN and RCNN are top and bottom performers on
contexts, respectively.
  By analyzing the results, we present our late fusion method, LF-COCO. LF-COCO
selects the appropriate depth strategy based on the context and thus gets a
robust performance on varying context. LF-COCO outperforms the state-of-the-art
by 3% on average on MS COCO test-dev.
  In source code, we provide a novel context sensitivity benchmark, code for
deep detector comparison based on the exploited context and our fusion code,
which is a simple but efficient fusion of single and two stage object
detectors.

for Wikipedia that organizes Wikipedia into a collection of graphs layered on
top of each other, learns complementary entity representations from their
topology and content, and combines them with a lightweight learning-to-rank
approach to recommend related entities on Wikipedia. Through offline and online
evaluations, we show that the resulting embeddings and recommendations perform
well in terms of quality and user engagement. Balancing simplicity and quality,
this framework provides default entity recommendations for English and other

Through experiments, we find that while all the layers we study are useful, the
topmost layer, which is based on Wikipedia categories, dominates the performance
of our default entity recommender. We argue that the success of the topmost layer
is due to its ability to group together entities from the same domain or
industry, even if they are not related in other ways such as co-authorship or
common text.

Tendentious Entity Recommender. Through offline evaluations, we show that our
algorithm successfully creates new layers that lead to better default
entity recommendations.

a major barrier in kidney
transplantation (KT). The increasing shortage of kidney donors has driven the
development of desensitization techniques to overcome this immunological
challenge. Compared with compatible KT, patients undergoing incompatible KTs
are more likely to experience rejection, infection, malignancy, and graft loss.
We study the optimal acceptance of possibly incompatible kidneys for individual
end-stage kidney disease patients. To capture the effect of incompatibility, we
propose a Markov Decision Process (MDP) model that explicitly includes
compatibility as a state variable. The resulting higher-dimensional model makes
it more challenging to analyze, but under suitable conditions, we derive
structural properties including control limit-type optimal policies that are
easy to compute and implement. Numerical examples illustrate the behavior of
the optimal policy under different mismatch levels and highlight the importance
of explicitly incorporating the incompatibility level into the acceptance
decision when desensitization therapy is an option.
  We validate our model by comparing it with existing single-kidney lifetime
equity (SKLE) approach and a recently proposed method based on the Expected
Utility of Kidney Transplant (EUKT) approach. Our model yields similar results
under the same assumptions as the comparisons, which justifies its complexity.
For instance, we show that the SKLE approach can be viewed as computing the
discounted sum of utilities under a certain set of optimal policies induced
from our model. Moreover, by explicitly incorporating the incompatibility level
into the acceptance decision, our model can lead to higher EUKT scores in
certain scenarios than the approach used in the EUKT method.
  In conclusion, our model provides a general framework for investigating the
kidney acceptance decision under various degrees of incompatibility. The
derived optimal policies are strong candidates for practical use in the KT
setting and can guide further research with data and/or machine learning methods
to refine transplant outcomes.

currently used in computational
linguistics rely on unary modalities to allow for the controlled application of
structural rules affecting word order and phrase structure. These controlled
structural operations give rise to derivational ambiguities that are missed by
the original Lambek Calculus or its pregroup simplification. Proposals for
compositional interpretation of extended Lambek Calculus in the compact closed
category of FVect and linear maps have been made, but in these proposals the
syntax-semantics mapping ignores the control modalities, effectively
restricting their role to the syntax. Our aim is to turn the modalities into
first-class citizens of the vectorial interpretation. Building on the
directional density matrix semantics, we extend the interpretation of the type
system with an extra spin density matrix space. The interpretation of proofs
then results in ambiguous derivations being tensored with orthogonal spin
states. Our method introduces a way of simultaneously representing co-existing
interpretations of ambiguous utterances, and provides a uniform framework for
the integration of lexical and derivational ambiguity.
  We show the correctness and fully expressiveness of our proposal by
formally proving the soundness and completeness of the proof system with the
controlled structural rules, and by providing an interpretation of a core
English grammar based on extended Lambek Calculus, which includes the controlled
structural operations of passivization and clefting. In the interpretation of
the grammar we pay particular attention to the representation of ambiguous
sentences, and we briefly discuss how our representation can be related to
ambiguity representations in Computational Linguistics.
  Finally, we generalize our proposal to multiple ambiguous interpretations of a
single utterance ranging across different languages, providing a way to
represent the linguistic relatedness between utterances across different
languages that can encode structural and lexical co-variance.
  Focusing on English and several other languages in Afro-Asiatic, Sino-Tibetan
and Mongolic, we provide a formalization of utterance ambiguities covering 12
languages and 55 linguistic types, providing a generalization of the general
tendency observed in the data that ambiguous types tend to be inherited
between languages.
  All the mathematical proofs and most of the linguistic evidence are
automatically extracted from large corpora of text by the tool
LingMatrixhttps://github.com/AndreasVergaridis/LingMatrix, which provides a
fully implemented framework for the induction of linguistic relatedness from
text data.

rationalizable behavior, where players learn to avoid iteratively dominated
actions. However, even in the basic setting of multiplayer general-sum games,
existing algorithms require a number of samples exponential in the number of
players to learn rationalizable equilibria under bandit feedback. This paper
develops the first line of efficient algorithms for learning rationalizable
Coarse Correlated Equilibria (CCE) and Correlated Equilibria (CE) whose sample
complexities are polynomial in all problem parameters including the number of
players. To achieve this result, we also develop a new efficient algorithm for
the simpler task of finding one rationalizable action under bandit feedback,
whose sample complexity substantially improves over the best prior results. Our
algorithms adapt the popular Mirror Descent (MD) framework to the setting of
multiplayer bandit games and analyze their theoretical properties. Experiments
demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our algorithms.
  As a key technical component, we reduce problems involving rationalizable
CCE and CE to smaller problems involving no-regret learning of arbitrary
values. However, existing algorithms reducing this problem to a number of
players' order of magnitude involves intricate constructions of rational
spectra, even under observable feedback (e.g., linear bandits). We develop a
new, simpler approach to solve these problems under both bandit and linear
feedback settings.
  Our results also show how to reduce the problem of finding one rationalizable
action to a smaller instance of finding one stable state in a monotone dynamic
on a directed acyclic graph, which has connections to many other problems in
multiagent learning and other fields.

defined on a social network is analysed. The underlying social network is
described by an Erd\H{o}s-R\'{e}nyi random graph but, during the course of the
epidemic, susceptible individuals connected to infectious neighbours may drop
or rewire such connections. Large population limits of the model are derived
giving both convergence results for the early branching process-like behaviour,
and, assuming a major outbreak, the main phase of the epidemic process which
converges to a deterministic model that is equivalent to a certain pair
approximation model. Law of large numbers results are also obtained for the
final size (i.e. total number of individuals infected) of a major outbreak. Two
results stand out (valid for a range of parameter set-ups): (i) the limiting
final fraction infected may be discontinuous in the infection rate $\lambda$ at
its threshold $\lambda_c$ (thus making a discrete jump from $0$ to a strictly
positive limit as $\lambda$ increases through $\lambda_c$) and (ii) for the
equivalent to the standard Reed-Frost model set-up, the limiting final fraction
infected equals the probability of an individual ever becoming infected, which
may also display a discrete jump as the infection rate increases through
$\lambda_c$.
  A simple modification involving a latent period is also considered and this
may make the final fraction infected continuous in the infection rate across
the epidemic threshold. The results from the analysis are illustrated by a
case study of the UK COVID-19 epidemic.

spin asymmetry, sensitive to the top
quark polarisation, in $t$-channel single top quark production is presented. It
is based on a sample of pp collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 8 TeV
corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 19.7 $\mathrm{fb^{-1}}$. A
high-purity sample of $t$-channel single top quark events with an isolated muon
is selected. Signal and background components are estimated using a fit to
data. A differential cross section measurement, corrected for detector effects,
of an angular observable sensitive to the top quark polarisation is performed.
The differential distribution is used to extract a top quark spin asymmetry of
$0.26 \pm 0.03 \textrm{(stat)} \pm 0.10 \textrm{(syst)}$, which is compatible
with a p-value of $4.6\%$ with the standard model prediction of 0.44.
\textit{Eventually}, a combination with a previous measurement of the
polarisation of the top quark in $t\bar{t}$ dilepton events is also presented.
The combined measurement increases the sensitivity to the $V_{tb}$ coupling
determination and leads to an updated measurement of the single top quark spin
asymmetry $0.24 \pm 0.02 \textrm{(stat)} \pm 0.05 \textrm{(syst)}$.

problems, making their application in the linearized framework troublesome.
Reynolds-averaged Navier Stokes (RANS) combustion models, however, prove to
circumvent this problem, which makes them suitable candidates for this purpose.
The RANS combustion models are linearized around the temporal mean flow of the
turbulent jet flame, which is obtained by LES. An a priori analysis shows that
a linearized RANS-Eddy Break Up (EBU) model is the best suited among all
investigated combustion models for the investigated set-up and reproduces with
high accuracy the fluctuations in heat release from the LES data. The linear
turbulent reacting jet flame is simulated using the linearized Navier Stokes
equations coupled with the linearized stochastic source term model, which is
required for the linearized RANS-EBU model. It is shown that the flame itself
moderates the amplification of the acoustic waves in the jet.

fluctuations in heat release from the LES data with a root mean square (rms) of
the global linearized reaction rate from the linear theory within 25 % of the
corresponding LES value. An a posteriori analysis, within the framework of the
linearized theory, shows that the rms of the acoustic pressure in the
combustion chamber is less than 50 Pa.

stochastic source term model, proves to be powerful enough to reproduce with
high accuracy the fluctuations in heat release from the LES data and is
therefore suitable for predicting the response of a turbulent reacting jet
flame to upstream acoustic actuation.

for NS primaries have recurrence times in excess of a decade for outbursts at

expected total population of NS LMXBs with the observed one and with the
millisecond radio pulsar (MSRP) population of the Galaxy, systems with

of these systems have yet been discovered.

completely wrong for NS LMXBs, the population of known long period bursters in

needing a splitter. In the proposed system model, a portion of the spectrum is
used for information decoding (ID) while the remaining portion is exploited for
energy harvesting (EH) in an orthogonal frequency division multiple access
(OFDMA) network. To investigate the performance gain, an optimization problem
is formulated that maximizes the harvested energy of a multi-user single-cell
OFDMA downlink (DL) network with SWIPT and also satisfies a minimum data-rate
requirement for all users. A locally optimal solution for the underlying
problem, which is essentially non-convex due to the coupling of the integer
variable, is obtained by using optimization tools. Second, the proposed system
model is improved in order to investigate the resource allocation problem of
needing to maximize throughput based on the separated receiver architecture in
an OFDMA multi-user multi-cell system that uses SWIPT. The resulting problem,
which jointly optimizes the subcarrier assignment and power allocation, is a
mixed-integer non-linear problem (MINLP), which is very challenging to solve
optimally due to its computational complexity. To deal with this difficulty,
efficient suboptimal algorithms that are decentralized and operate in an
independent and non-cooperative fashion among the APs are developed in order to
facilitate joint resource allocation with fast convergence. In addition, the
convergence of the proposed subcarrier allocation (SA) and power allocation

function, the derivatives, and the step size. Moreover, the performance of the
proposed SA and PA schemes is evaluated through extensive numerical results
that also compare with joint SA and PA approaches in order to substantiate the
effectiveness and the gain of the proposed strategies in terms of throughput.

language, words of the same form can take different meanings depending on
context. While humans easily infer the meaning or gloss of such words based on
their surrounding words and grammatical contexts as well as general
knowledge, machines face difficulty in doing so. In this paper, we reconsider
the problem of Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD), which is the task of identifying
the proper gloss for a word (also called sense) in a given context. In
particular, we focus on the Levin et al. dataset which contains phrases in
which the main word is missing and needs to be recovered. Related tasks such as
fill-in-the-blank generation can be seen as applications of this dataset. We
propose a simple yet effective neural approach to this problem. The core idea
behind our approach is that contexts are related to their corresponding
 completions. For example, the phrase "I'll have the same as" typically
accompanies the word "coffee". Thus our model learns to represent contexts in
a way that is similar to their corresponding completions. We show through
various experiments that our approach is superior to previous methods. In
particular, our approach is able to better capture general knowledge as well as
long range dependencies in contexts.
  We also study different aspects of the task of WSD. In one experiment, we
study the effect of domain on WSD. We train a model on a general domain
dataset, and test it on a medical domain dataset. Interestingly, our model
shows a significant improvement when tested on medical contexts, showing
that while the model has learned a general language representation from the
general domain dataset, it also retains information that is relevant to
medical contexts. In another experiment, we study the effect of disambiguation
data quality on a model's performance. We test a model on datasets of varying
quality (i.e. more noisy labeling) and show that the model's performance
degrades as the quality of the data gets worse.

paper, we present a first-of-its-kind study on the problem of sequential
knowledge reasoning over multimodal procedures. Specifically, we study if
language models can learn to reason about a set of kitchen procedures whose
descriptions are communicated through both texts and images. To evaluate models'

sequence understanding tasks into pairwise comparison evaluation metrics. Our
experiments show that multimodal language models suffer from several issues
including over-reliance on visual noise, failure to attend to relevant visual
information, and inability to update visual information efficiently. These issues
lead to poor performance compared to text-only models and a simple visual

of disks surrounding young stars have shown that their morphology is made of
azimuthally-symmetric or point-symmetric substructures, in some cases with
spiral arms, localized spur- or crescent-shaped features. The majority of
theoretical studies with the aim of interpreting the observational results have
focused on disk models with planets, under the assumption that the disk
substructures are due to the disk-planet interaction. However, so far only in
very few cases exoplanets have been detected in these systems. Furthermore,
some substructures are expected to appear \textit{before} planets form, as they
are necessary to drive the concentration of small solids which can lead to the
formation of planetesimals. In this work we present observational predictions
from high-resolution 3D radiative hydrodynamical models which follow the
evolution of gas and solids in a protoplanetary disk. We focus on substructures
in the distribution of millimeter-sized and smaller solid particles produced by
the vertical shear instability. We show that their characteristics are
compatible with some of the shallow gaps detected in recent observations at
sub-mm/mm wavelengths, and present predictions for future observations with
better sensitivity and angular resolution with ALMA and a Next Generation Very
Large Array.
  We predict that shallow substructures due to the vertical shear instability
will be more common than deep gaps in terms of the location of substructures on
the disk, and that gas and solid particles will not always be filtered out of
the gaps. While the latter is a common assumption in recent observations
attempting to constrain the presence of planets, it is not universally
valid.
  Finally, we emphasize that the VSI-driven substructures are not stationary
features. Both further observation and careful comparison of models with
observation are crucial to fully understand the dynamics of protoplanetary
disks.
  Based on the predicted characteristics of substructures formed by the VSI,
we suggest that the lack of exoplanets does not necessarily mean that
planets are not needed to explain observed substructures in disks. Further
observation is crucial to fully constrain the role of planet-disk
interactions and disk-gas-solids interactions in the formation of substructures
in protoplanetary disks.
  We also suggest that further theoretical work is needed to fully understand
how substructures formed by the VSI may lead to the concentration of smaller
solids and the formation of planetesimals.

on a linear chain of trapped ions, using Gaussian amplitude modulation and a
constant laser frequency. We select this frequency to balance the entanglement
accumulation of all motional modes during the gate to produce a strong
robustness to frequency error, even for long ion chains. We demonstrate this
technique on a three-ion chain, achieving $<\,1\%$ reduction from peak fidelity
over a $20\,$kHz range of frequency offset, and we analyze the performance of
this gate design through numerical simulations on chains of two to 33 ions.
Ultimately, the robustness of frequency to the length of the ion chain makes this
technique well-suited to the QNL scaling of quantum computation, where long ion
chains will be necessary.
  From a technical perspective, this work also represents an important step
towards the implementation of a full quantum computation with MBQC, as it
includes two important components: (a) it produces entanglement between any two
qubit codes (i.e. logical qubits), and (b) it has a high fidelity ($>98\%$) on a
three-qubit code that includes an MMQ (Molmer-Sorensen) gate as part of its
entanglement generation process.
  We show that the main challenge in implementing frequency-robust gates is
the trade-off between the motional modes that are affected by the laser frequency
and the steady-state of the ion's motional mode that is used to decode the
quantum computation (typically near zero in amplitude). In the case of the
Molmer-Sorensen gate, a lower laser frequency results in an increase in the
amplitude of the steady-state of the ion's motional mode, which makes it easier
to decode, but it also results in the slow entanglement accumulation of some
motional modes that are sensitive to frequency, causing a reduction in
frequency robustness. On the other hand, a higher laser frequency results in the
fast entanglement accumulation of these modes, resulting in a higher variance in
the number of photons trapped between the two qubit codes, which motivates the
use of Gaussian state decoding. Note that this variance can come from motional
modes that are not affected by the laser frequency, reducing the requirement on

common concern raised from ex-post assessments is that storage resources can
fail to respond to strong price signals during times of scarcity. While
commonly attributed to forecast error or failures in operations, we posit that
this behavior can be explained from the perspective of risk-averse scheduling.
Using a stochastic self-scheduling framework and real-world data harvested from
the Australian National Electricity Market, we demonstrate that risk-averse
storage resources tend to have a myopic operational perspective, that is, they
typically engage in near-term price arbitrage and chase only few extreme price
spikes and troughs, thus remaining idle in several time periods with markedly
high and low prices. This has important policy implications given the
non-transparency of unit risk aversion and apparent need for market designs
incorporating risk attributes of resources.
  We further show that storage resources have different risk profiles across
different days of the week and holidays versus weekends, among other factors,
which can impact their ability to engage in flexible dispatch across different
days. Finding appropriate risk-adjusted metrics of variability can help
capture such risk profiles and allow for more informed self-scheduling
decisions by storage resources, as well as better risk management and market
designs that take into account storage's risk behavior.
  Finally, our results stress the importance of jointly considering forecast
error and unit risk aversion for any future assessments of storage resources --
assessments that can lead to better risk management strategies and market
designs, ultimately resulting in more efficient outcomes in the real market.
Moreover, avowed risk modeling in storage operations and policy makers must
consider risk aversion and its impacts on storage's risk profiles and
performance.

University of Hamburg's Portable University Model for the Atmosphere with
simplified (linear) boundary layer friction, a Newtonian cooling scheme and dry
convective adjustment. A series of controlled experiments are conducted by
varying planetary rotation rate and imposed equator-to-pole temperature
difference. These defining parameters are cast into dimensionless forms to
establish a parameter space, in which most experiments fall into one of five
distinct regimes: (i) a nearly barotropic flow with an mid-latitude jet at a
sufficiently high latitudes; (ii) a baroclinic wave-generating regime with a
low-latitude jet; (iii) a regime of extreme planetary wave activity with a
high-latitude jet; (iv) a dry, strongly ventilated stratosphere with a very
high-latitude jet and little wave activity; and (v) a stratospheric
thermosphere with a very high-latitude jet and strong planetary wave activity

explicit manipulation of the stratospheric temperature and related
ventilation, while the convective adjustment prevents the development of
unrealistic, intense mid-latitude temperature gradients. The presentation
focuses on the differences between the regimes and the relevant controlling
factors. The results are not directly compared to modern Earth observations,
but rather as idealized simulations that explore the limits of possible

context of graph-structured data. We discuss the formulations of DP applicable
to the publication of graphs and their associated statistics as well as machine
learning on graph-based data, including graph neural networks (GNNs). The
formulation of DP in the context of graph-structured data is challenging, as
individual data points are interconnected (often non-linearly or sparsely).
This non-locality complicates the computation of individual privacy loss in
differentially private learning. While there is an extensive body of research on
GNNs, we aim to take a first step in providing a conceptual foundation for a
comprehensive privacy analysis of GNNs by studying the underlying problems and
formulations involved. To this end, we provide an exhaustive discussion on the
definitions of DP applicable to graph release and learning on graphs, which
includes a discussion of the difficulties arising from non-locality. We conclude
with open problems and important challenges in this area.

talking about the definitions of DP applicable to graph release and learning on

non-locality. We give an overview of different applications, such as the
publication of node attributes and graph structure, the learning of private
GNNs and the application of DP to game theory. Furthermore, we emphasize the
importance of composability in DP and discuss applications and challenges in
the context of graph-structured data.

simulating the otherwise difficult-to-compute dynamics of quantum many-body
systems. In this work we derive, within the positive-P phase-space formalism, a
new stochastic hydrodynamic method for the description of interacting Bose
gases. It goes beyond existing hydrodynamic approaches, such as superfluid
hydrodynamics or generalized hydrodynamics, in its capacity to simulate the
full quantum dynamics of these systems: it possesses the ability to compute
non-equilibrium quantum correlations, even for short-wavelength phenomena.
Using this description, we derive a linearized stochastic hydrodynamic scheme
which is able to simulate such non-equilibrium situations for longer times than
the full positive-P approach, at the expense of approximating the treatment of
quantum fluctuations, and show that this linearized scheme can be directly
connected with existing Bogoliubov approaches. Furthermore, we go on to
demonstrate the usefulness and advantages of this formalism by exploring the
correlations that arise in a quantum shock wave scenario and comparing its
predictions to other established quantum many-body approaches.
  We find that, in the case of the shock wave, the linearized scheme is able
to capture the emergence of quasi-momentum modes which are responsible for the
formation of the sonic-boomerang phenomenon. Furthermore, it is able to
predict the same mass transport profiles as the full positive-P approach, but
for a much larger duration of time. Moreover, it is able to reproduce the
string-like behavior of the width of the sonic-boomerang, which is known to
be an important indicator of quantum effects in the overlap of two
condensates. Finally, we show that the stochastic nature of the full positive-P
description is crucial for the generation of correlations in the overlap of
two condensates.

observed in the edge plasma of the JET tokamak. Although PTMs are well
documented, little is known about the mechanisms which produce these
structures. In the case of the PTM, an ELM-postcursor, its genesis is usually

the appearance of a seed magnetic island which evolves into a PTM later. In
this study we try to invoke a creation mechanism based on the concepts and
observations in edge plasma turbulence. An interesting aspect of plasma
turbulence is the occurrence of coherent, long-lived structures in the
scrape-off-layer (SOL). These localized and magnetic-field-aligned regions with
higher or lower plasma densities are called blobs and holes. Measurements show
that these filaments carry parallel currents. We thus here interpret
ELM-filaments as massive blobs and the interspace between these filaments as
holes. We demonstrate that a forward-modelled closed current filament on a q=3
surface produces similar magnetic fluctuations as measured by the JET in-vessel
magnetic pickup coils if a PTM is present. From that we deduce that if a hole
is captured on a q=3 surface after an ELM-crash, a PTM equivalent signature is
generated. If the ELM-filament itself is captured on a q=3 surface, a
closed current filament is produced which persists longer than the ELM-filament
itself. If the ELM-filament is reflected from a q=3 surface, a PTM is produced
on that surface in the case if the hole captured on that surface is
sufficiently large. Based on these three scenarios we can explain all
observations of PTMs in the JET data.

cannot be applied to the palm tree mode structures observed in the JET data.
Instead we can explain all observations by assuming that these filaments are
carried by the turbulent ELM-filaments and holes. Based on that we deduce that
the origin of the palm tree mode is the same as that of ELM-filaments, i.e. the
convective drift turbulence.

filament captured on a q=3 surface can be explained by a sequence of
successive filaments and holes.

number of continual learning methods based on pretrained models have been
proposed. Some of these methods design continual learning mechanisms on the
pre-trained representations and only allow minimum updates or even no updates
of the backbone models during the training of continual learning. In this
paper, we question whether the complexity of these models is needed to achieve
good performance by comparing them to a simple baseline that we designed. We
argue that the pretrained feature extractor itself can be strong enough to
achieve a competitive or even better continual learning performance on
Split-CIFAR100 and CoRe 50 benchmarks. To validate this, we conduct a very
simple baseline that 1) use the frozen pretrained model to extract image
features for every class encountered during the continual learning stage and
compute their corresponding mean features on training data, and 2) predict the
class of the input based on the nearest neighbor distance between test samples
and mean features of the classes; i.e., Nearest Mean Classifier (NMC). This
baseline is single-headed, exemplar-free, and can be task-free (by updating the
means continually). This baseline achieved 88.53% on 10-Split-CIFAR-100,
surpassing the current state-of-the-art. Our empirical study shows that the
pretrained feature extractor, combined with a simple classifier, can achieve
competitive or even better continual learning performance on Split-CIFAR100 and
CoRe 50 benchmarks.
  Which means there is no need for all the complexity in the current state-of-the-art
continual learning methods any more. We hope our findings could give a fresh
perspective to the research community in designing simpler models for
continual learning.

and Shmaya introduced the class of
$\lambda$-Lipschitz games in which every player's payoff function is
$\lambda$-Lipschitz with respect to the actions of the other players. They
showed that such games admit $\epsilon$-approximate pure Nash equilibria for
certain settings of $\epsilon$ and $\lambda$. They left open, however, the
question of how hard it is to find such an equilibrium. In this work, we
develop a query-efficient reduction from more general games to Lipschitz games.
We use this reduction to show a query lower bound for any algorithm finding an
$\epsilon$-approximate pure Nash equilibrium of $n$-player, $m$-action Lipschitz
games in time worse than $\Omega(n^2/\epsilon^2)$. Combined with a
polynomial-time finding algorithm for special classes of Lipschitz games (e.g.,
two-player games and games with linear payoffs), our lower bound complements
completely the existing upper-bound proof.

for games with mixed strategic support, significantly improving upon existing
algorithms. We show its utility with a tighter hardness proof for finding
pure equilibria.
  Finally, we introduce the class of games with maximal range of payoffs -- a
natural generalization of the class of Lipschitz games. We show a natural
connection between such games and pure Nash equilibria, and prove a lower bound
for finding such an equilibrium even in games with two actions and pure payoffs.
Together, our results broaden the supply of natural lower bounds for algorithms
finding pure Nash equilibria.

a popular method for estimating the true
performance of machine learning models, allowing model selection and parameter
tuning. However, the very process of CV requires random partitioning of the
data and so our performance estimates are in fact stochastic, with variability
that can be substantial for natural language processing tasks. In this paper,
we systematically explore the effect of different K-fold CV settings on
performance estimation for both model selection and parameter tuning. Our
findings demonstrate that different CV settings can result in significantly
different performance estimates, meaning that the very process of performance
estimation is non-deterministic. We offer a number of practical recommendations
for CV settings in order to make the process more deterministic while still
maintaining the effectiveness of CV.
  We further argue that current ways of tuning parameters using K-fold CV can
lead to over-estimation of performance on unseen data because the evaluation on
the held-out test data is done only once after all parameters have been tried.
To address this issue, we propose a simple way of performing ensemble using
multiple performances estimated through leave-one-out CV (LOOCV) to get a more
realistic estimate of performance. Finally, we show through experiments that
while the basic method of performance estimation via LOOCV was first proposed
over 40 years ago, it remains little used in machine learning, likely due to
overemphasis on K-fold CV. With the rise of large models that require extensive
tuning time, we believe it is time to reconsider LOOCV.

simulations, which currently do not accurately reflect the overall trends in
observed binary separations.

assumption of a constant $\beta$ is equivalent to a force balance between the
binaries and the envelope. This result may be useful for further investigating
the relations between $\beta$, and binary and stellar properties. However,
measuring the small expected values of $\beta$ may be difficult.

that allows for a better understanding of the connection between AIM
simulations and observed binary separations, which are the subject of a
follow-up paper.

as having some aspects of force balance during CE evolution, with the main

physical and observational properties of binaries that are in or have been in

Existing methods typically insert actors into the scene according to a set of
hand-crafted heuristics and are limited in their ability to model the true
complexity and diversity of real traffic scenes, thus inducing a content gap
between synthesized traffic scenes compared to real ones. As a result, existing
methods fail to learn scene understanding and scene safety from real data
incorporating synthetic negatives. To address this content gap, we propose a
novel continuous diffusion-based actor insertion process that generates actor
positions and velocities that are consistent with the scene's semantic map and
video stream. From a starting distribution of isolated actors, our method
gradually inserts them into a virtual world until a complex traffic scene is
established. We demonstrate how this allows for semi-synthetic datasets that
look like real data to you but contain no real actors, thus enabling learning
methods to validate their performance on real data incorporating synthetic
negatives.
  We evaluate our method through quantitative analysis of whether inserted
actors drive in a manner consistent with real traffic and through case-study
style qualitative analysis to show that the overall quality of the scenes
generated is also very high.
  We hope that by studying continuous actor insertion, researchers will be able
to generate high-quality, semi-synthetic datasets for safety evaluation and
testing, thus helping to accelerate the adoption of computer vision-based
safety-critical systems.

time-dependent partial differential equations (PDEs) is the ability to preserve
certain properties of the continuum solution, such as associated conservation
laws or other geometric structures of the solution. There is a long history of
the development and analysis of such structure-preserving discretisation
schemes, including both proofs that standard schemes have structure-preserving
properties and proposals for novel schemes that achieve both high-order
accuracy and exact preservation of certain properties of the continuum
differential equation. When coupled with implicit time-stepping methods, a
major downside to these schemes is that their structure-preserving properties
generally rely on exact solution of the (possibly nonlinear) systems of
equations defining each time-step in the discrete scheme. Since a significant
proportion of the computational cost of a time-dependent simulation is typically
devoted to the solution of the discrete time-step equations, this means that
most structure-preserving schemes are currently not computationally efficient
enough to be widely used. In order to address this problem, we develop a
general algorithm for locally repairing approximate (linear or multilinear)
time-step operators to guarantee that they preserve the desired properties of
the continuum differential equation. The resulting schemes have natural
multigrid properties and can be used as components of computationally efficient
solutions to problems involving time-dependent PDEs of arbitrary order in space
and time.
  We present a new higher-order time-stepping method for the time-dependent
linearised compressible Euler equations that accurately preserves several
important properties of the exact solution to the differential equation. In
particular the method conserves the mean-intensity, reshapes the reshaping
tensor and normalises the normalisation vector, and provides a direct constraint
on the normalised magnitude of perturbations to the intensity and tensor. These
properties are important for the reliable modelling of the dynamics of
short-wavelength instabilities such as those that lead to transonic
galactic-glass patterns. The method is derived from a new fourth-order
structure-preserving time-stepping algorithm for systems of ordinary differential
equations that is presented in a companion paper. The new time-stepping
algorithm is shown there to be obtained from a direct discretisation of a
higher-order time-dependent transport equation for the Eulerian linearised
compressible fluid. The new time-stepping algorithm is posted in a form that can
be readily implemented into existing time-stepping based solvers for the
compressible Euler equations.

  Let $Q \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be a non-constant polynomial and let $\delta > 0$ be
a real number. We say that $Q$ is $\delta$-strongly joint ergodic if for an
collection of sequences $F_1, \ldots, F_k : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ with

real numbers $\alpha_i$ with $\prod_{i=1}^k \alpha_i = \delta$, and a
non-negative real number $c_0$ it holds that for every ergodic system $(X,T)$
we have $$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} F_1(n) A_1(n) +
\ldots + F_k(n) A_k(n) = \prod_{i=1}^k \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=
0}^{N-1} F_i(n) A_i(n),$$ where $A_i(n) = \int_X f_i \circ T^{Q(n)} d\mu,$
for some $L^2$-functions $f_i : X \to \mathbb{C}.$ If $\delta > 0,$ then $Q$ is
$\delta$-strongly joint ergodic if it is $\delta'$-strongly joint ergodic for
some $\delta' \geq \delta.$

certain distance from an observer, e.g., $>$50m. Far3Det is particularly
important for autonomous vehicles (AVs) operating at highway speeds, which
require detections of far-field obstacles to ensure sufficient braking
distances. However, contemporary AV benchmarks such as nuScenes underemphasize
this problem because they evaluate performance only up to a certain distance
(50m). One reason is that obtaining far-field 3D annotations is difficult,
particularly for lidar sensors that produce a very large number of point clouds
far away from the vehicle. In this work we develop a new benchmark, FarSide,
dedicated to the Far3Det task. We design a data collection protocol that
minimizes annotation of unnecessary point clouds and enables efficient
lidar-based far-field 3D object detection training. We also introduce methods
for evaluating Far3Det performance at various braking scenarios. Our results
show that contemporary Far3Det models underperform a simple baseline that
ignores far-field annotations. We highlight the importance of designing
benchmarks tailored to specific AV scenarios and validate the efficacy of our
benchmark through various experiments.

costs reasonable. Our protocol prioritizes annotating point clouds that are
likely to project onto visible images, thus improving the quality of the
annotations and making image-lidar sensor training relevant to the real-world

leverage domain randomization to enhance the diversity of the logged data. We
validate the effectiveness of our data logging protocol through detection

a novel technique for automatically
learning system call filtering policies for containerized microservices
applications. At run-time, Timeloops automatically learns which system calls a
program should be allowed to invoke while rejecting attempts to call other
system calls that are spurious to the program's correct execution. Timeloops
does so efficiently by training a very small, application-specific call
white-list at startup time based on static program analysis of the application
's source code and its dependencies. We demonstrate that the resulting
techniques significantly reduce the attack surface of microservices applications
while preserving their performance.
  We present a new language-independent taint-based static analysis technique
that reverses the control flow of a program to identify which system calls a
program is allowed to invoke while executing a particular input. We show how
this technique can be used to generate very effective call filtering policies
for microservices applications. We then introduce a lightweight dynamic
technique that efficiently prunes the set of system calls that a program
potentially invokes as a result of interacting with its inputs. We show that
the resulting filtering policies obtained by combining our static and dynamic
analysis techniques are much more effective at filtering out spurious system
calls than dynamic analysis alone.
  Timeloops addresses three important challenges associated with automatically
generating system call filtering policies for microservices applications.
First, a microservices program typically consists of more than one language
(e.g., C++ and Python) which complicates the policy generation. Second, many
open-source libraries are often used to implement common utilities such as
networking, persistence, and cryptographic operations that, in turn, may
invoke unwanted system calls depending on how they are used by the application;
and finally, many microservices applications are designed to parse and
generate various file formats (e.g., JSON, XML, and binary) which require
interactions with the file system that can lead to spurious system calls.
  At run-time, Timeloops efficiently learns which system calls a program should
be allowed to call while rejecting spurious system calls by constructing a
very small, application-specific call white-list at startup time based on
static program analysis of the application's source code and its dependencies.
We demonstrate that the resulting techniques significantly reduce the attack
surface of microservices applications while preserving their performance.
  We evaluate our approach with 12 real-world microservices applications that
interact with network, files, cryptographic services, and parse various
file formats such as JSON and XML.

Standard Model (SM) is well-motivated since anomaly cancellations require the

pseudo-Goldstone boson dark matter (DM) scenario in which the imaginary

DM relic density is determined by the SM Higgs boson mediated process, but its
elastic scattering with nucleons through the exchange of Higgs bosons is highly
suppressed due to its pseudo-Goldstone boson nature. The model is therefore
free from the constraints arising from direct DM detection experiments. We
identify regions of the model parameter space for reproducing the observed DM

validity of using the unitarity bound on the $B-L$ boson mass is discussed in
the context of the $B-L$ extended SM. Using the energy scale at which the

a new particle called a majoron. We identify a unique region of the model

study the joint effect of
immigration and a competition-dispersal tradeoff in the dynamics of two species
competing for space in regular lattices. Individuals of one species can invade
a nearest-neighbor site in the lattice, while individuals of the other species
are able to invade sites at any distance but are less competitive locally,
i.e., they establish with a probability $g \le 1$. The model also accounts for
immigration, modeled as an external noise that may spontaneously replace an
individual at a lattice site by another individual of the other species. This
combination of mechanisms gives rise to a rich variety of outcomes for species
competition, including exclusion of either species, mono-stable coexistence of
both species at different population proportions, and bi-stable coexistence
with proportions of populations that depend on the initial condition.
Remarkably, in the bi-stable phase, the system undergoes a discontinuous
transition as the intensity of immigration overcomes a threshold, leading to a
half loop dynamics associated to a cusp catastrophe, which causes the
irreversible loss of the species with the shortest dispersal range.
Simultaneously, the mono-stable coexistence transition is continuous, and is
associated to a usual tipping point. The model accounts for the important
effects of a trade-off between competition and dispersal on the dynamics of the
two species.
  Our model has direct implications for the study of invasive species and
species competing for space in regular lattices throughout the world. In
particular, the bi-stable phase may account for coexistence of two species of
different degrees of invasiveness and competitiveness, as observed in various
real-world examples, such as the coexistence of monarch and viceroy butterflies
and the agave plant and the yucca moth in deserts in the Americas.
  Finally, the bi-stable dynamics presented by our model is analogous to the
real-world situations in which the coexistence of species with apparently
incompatible traits is observed, and thus our model can be used as a theoretical
framework to build case studies on the competition and coexistence of species
throughout the world.

important. We also observe that all the algorithms converge fast. It takes at

MLPs) make powerful functional representations for

data often increases in density as new dimensions are added which can be

A growing neural network has a fixed input dimensionality, limiting its ability
to capture density changes in new dimensions. In this paper, we propose a
Meta-Functional Representation Model that uses MLPs to model density as a
function of input density in the feature space. We learn a mapping from the
feature space to a functional representation of density in a meta-learning
framework. Our model is compact, scalable, and generalizable to new related
domains. Experiments on both synthetic and real world datasets shows that our
model achieves higher accuracy and lower prediction time compared to

animals contain animal-diagnostic features. By contrast, the agency hypothesis

perpendicular to the line-of-sight, Bperp, in vector magnetic field maps is
discussed. Previous works on this topic have illustrated that the problem
exists; here we perform novel comparisons between independently derived
Bperp maps, and maps reconstructed from tomographic reconstructions of the
vector magnetic field, obtained via the Minimum Current Mass Principle (MCM
principle). Data come from the Solar Dynamics Observatory/UVC2 observations of
the April 16, 2014 coronal mass ejection event, over the box $|-75^\circ,
75^\circ| \times |-75^\circ, 75^\circ|$ in solar coordinates. We test two
methods for the MCM principle, namely Minimize Current Density and
Minimize-Current-Magnitude. We show that both methods are able to reconstruct
the background field with high accuracy, recovering also large scale structures
such as coronal arcs. However, we find that both methods have a positive Bperp
bias, with the average absolute bias ranging from 10-20 G. The comparison between
independent line-of-sight magnetograms also shows a bias, in agreement with
previous works, but the analysis is limited by the lack of 3D reconstructions
of the full vector field. Finally, we test the impact of the bias on the
identification of coronal sources, finding that it leads to overestimation of
the brightness of small hot structures, such as coronal bright points and the
base of coronal mass ejections.
  Based on our results, we suggest that a simple de-trending of Bperp by -10 G
is a reasonable first step towards obtaining more reliable maps of this
component. Future work will be dedicated to quantitatively assessing the
quality of Bperp maps, with a particular focus on constructing robust
benchmarks.
  We discuss the implications of the bias for the study of coronal
heating/dimming and its link with magnetic fine structure.
  Finally, we emphasize that the MCM principle, being a field-based method,
provides a natural way to address this issue, in contrast with current density
based methods.
  Novel comparisons with THOSTEQUATOR maps are also presented in the appendix.
  We suggest that the community will greatly benefit from a thorough and
well-documented comparison between different methods for the reconstruction of
the vector magnetic field.

models to interpret these age trends, finding that high-mass clusters are more
likely to be not tidally limited and expand. We also find that most clusters in

finding a large scatter that appears to decrease with cluster age. The youngest
clusters have a typical surface density of 100 $M_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$.

cross-task generalization.

long way to go -- they can only achieve around 10% performance of the models
trained with supervised data. This indicates there is a corpus gap, i.e.,
popular web corpora usually contain too many topics unrelated to the target
tasks, leading to the poor performance of unsupervised cross-task
generalization. We hope our findings can encourage the community to collect or
generate more domain-specific corpora for unsupervised cross-task

the status of requirements engineering
in the gaming industry. Recent papers in the area were surveyed.
Characterizations of the gaming industry were deliberated upon by portraying
its relations with the market industry. Some research directions in the area of
requirements engineering in the gaming industry were also mentioned.
  In the market industry, products are designed to sell; the sales process
determines the product's requirements. On the other hand, in the gaming
industry, the requirements are determined by the design and development
processes; the sales (that is, the revenue) is a secondary concern. This
difference leads to several interesting implications for requirements
engineering in the gaming industry.
  Several games companies were surveyed. Their home pages, news articles
concerning them, and some of their financial reports available at the
Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) site were examined. Its development
processes were also deliberated upon by portraying the roles of project
managers, designers, and engineers in it. Some interesting implications for
requirements engineering in the gaming industry were presented based on the
characterizations of the gaming industry and its development process.
  Several interesting research topics in the area of requirements engineering
for games were identified. For example, a theoretical framework or theory of
the genre of a game would be very useful. Today such a framework or theory
does not exist. Also, several empirical studies on the development processes
for games are needed.
  In conclusion, the gaming industry is a very interesting and rewarding
domain for requirements engineering research. Its unique characteristics and
development processes offer many opportunities for interesting research
topics.
  This work is an extension of our earlier work (Sajid, 1999). In Sajid (1999)
we presented an overview of the gaming industry, its development process for
requirements engineering, and some implications of the gaming industry's
market for its development. Here we present an account of the status of
requirements engineering in the gaming industry through a survey of several
games companies and present several interesting implications of the gaming
industry's market for its development. Also, several interesting research
topics for requirements engineering in the gaming industry are identified.
Relevant literature in the area of requirements engineering for games is
discussed and several interesting issues in it are pointed out. Finally, we
conclude that the gaming industry is a very interesting and rewarding domain
for requirements engineering research. Its unique characteristics and
development processes offer many opportunities for interesting research
topics.

world.In China, COVID-19 has caused severe consequences. Many cities have been
locked down to control the pandemic. The online healthcare platform has seen a
sharp increase in demand due to the shortage of medical resources. Two types of
fraudulent behaviors occurred on the online healthcare platform during that
period, which are (1) online healthcare fraud and (2) drug fraud. The first
type of fraud occurs when the fraudulent user (FU) registers multiple
fake identities (e.g., by using fake names and birthdays) to illegally
purchase more online healthcare services. The second type of fraud occurs when
the FU purchases the wrong medicines by providing incorrect order details.
Both of the fraudulent behaviors can be committed by the registered
identities after the registration process. Therefore, our goal is to reduce the
probability of both types of fraudulent behaviors during the purchase
process.To achieve this goal, our approach first collects the purchasing
behavior of all identities. Then it uses an unsupervised clustering algorithm
called DBSCAN to group the order details (e.g., medicine name, quantity,
address, etc.). After that our system checks for the outlier orders in each
cluster. If an outlier order is found in a cluster, our system sends an
alert to the platform administrator. Finally, our system uses a collaborative
filtering-based algorithm to suggest the possible categories of medicines
appropriate for the upcoming order of the user. With the suggested categories
of medicines, the user is less likely to commit the second type of fraudulent
behavior. To evaluate our approach, we collected the data of 31,972 online
healthcare purchases made by 17,440 identities over two years. From this
data, our approach identified 1,441 fraudulent orders with an average rate of
3.57%. This rate is about 70% higher than the previous studies. From this
data, our clustering-based outlier detection (COID) algorithm outperforms the
state-of-the-art Isolating Fraudulent Identities (IFID) algorithm by about
25%. Furthermore, our filtering-based suggestion (FBS) protocol also outperforms
the state-of-the-art collaborative filtering (CF) algorithm by about 21%. The
results demonstrate that our cooperative analysis of purchasing behaviors of
all identities, effective outlier detection algorithm, and appropriate
filtering-based suggestion technique make our approach successful in
preventing the two types of fraudulent behaviors from occurring

chanical modeling of the
strain-induced crystallization in unfilled polymers. This phenomenon
significantly influences mechanical and thermal properties of polymers and has
to be taken into consideration when planning manufacturing processes as well as
applications of the final product. In order to simultaneously capture both
kinds of effects, the model proposed starts by introducing a state variable
equation for the conversion from the vitrified to the crystalline state.
Subsequently, Hookean behavior is assumed in the sense of Kirchhoff for both
amorphous and crystalline phases whereas the conversion function depends on the
deformation history. Thermomechanical relations close the proposed model and
allow for the simulation of thermally induced crystallization as well as
mechanically induced crystallization at constant temperature. It is demonstrated
how the proposed approach can be implemented into a finite element program and
used to investigate a prototypical polymer part undergoing mechanical and
thermal loading.

difficulty of requiring optimal state action demonstrations limits the space of
